Mid-domain null model of richness along a gradient

Source: R/mde.R
range_mde.Rd

If species' ranges are placed at random within a bounded gradient, they overlap most in the middle, so richness peaks at mid-gradient even with no environmental cause: the mid-domain effect (Colwell and Hurtt 1994; Colwell and Lees 2000). range_mde() builds this null model from the observed ranges, in the spirit of RangeModel (Colwell 2008), and compares it with the observed richness at each site.

Each species keeps its observed range size (the number of consecutive sampled sites it spans, after range_through() interpolation), and its position is randomised:

  • model = "uniform": every position where the range fits is equally likely (Colwell and Hurtt 1994). The expected richness is computed exactly; the interval comes from nsim randomisations.

  • model = "spread": the range starts at a random site and spreads to random neighbouring sites (the "spreading dye" model of Jetz and Rahbek 2001, as in the rangemodelR package), which places more ranges near the ends than the uniform model.

Sites are treated as positions in order along the gradient, so the model assumes the sampled sites represent the domain evenly.

Usage

range_mde(
  data,
  gradient,
  site = site,
  species = species,
  model = c("uniform", "spread"),
  nsim = 999,
  conf = 0.95,
  interpolate = TRUE,
  .by = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'td_mde'
glance(x, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format, with one row per record.

gradient

Column with the position of each site on the gradient (one value per site).

site, species

<tidy-select> The column holding site identifiers and the column holding species names.

model

"uniform" or "spread".

nsim

Number of randomisations.

conf

Width of the simulation interval.

interpolate

Apply range_through() first (recommended).

.by

<tidy-select> Optional grouping columns, kept in the output. Grouped data frames are also respected.

x

A range_mde() result.

...

Not used.

Value

A tibble of class td_mde with the grouping columns, the site and gradient columns, observed richness, expected richness under the null model, its sd, lower and upper simulation limits, and outside ("above", "below" or "within"). Attributes r2 (the variance in observed richness explained by the null model, one value per group) and p_value (a global test: the proportion of randomisations that deviate from the expectation at least as much as the observed richness) summarise the fit; see glance().

References

Colwell, R. K. and Hurtt, G. C. (1994). Nonbiological gradients in species richness and a spurious Rapoport effect. American Naturalist, 144, 570-595. doi:10.1086/285695

Colwell, R. K. and Lees, D. C. (2000). The mid-domain effect: geometric constraints on the geography of species richness. Trends in Ecology & Evolution, 15, 70-76. doi:10.1016/S0169-5347(99)01767-X

Colwell, R. K. (2008). RangeModel: tools for exploring and assessing geometric constraints on species richness (the mid-domain effect) along transects. Ecography, 31, 4-7. doi:10.1111/j.2008.0906-7590.05347.x

Jetz, W. and Rahbek, C. (2001). Geometric constraints explain much of the species richness pattern in African birds. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 98, 5661-5666. doi:10.1073/pnas.091100998

Examples

set.seed(1)
mde <- range_mde(png_frogs, gradient = elevation, nsim = 199)
mde
#> # A tibble: 8 × 8
#>   site   elevation observed expected    sd lower upper outside
#>   <chr>      <int>    <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <chr>  
#> 1 MW0200       200       13     7.65  2.65  4     14   within 
#> 2 MW0700       700       13    11.8   2.73  6.95  17   within 
#> 3 MW1200      1200       17    13.7   3.13  8     21   within 
#> 4 MW1700      1700       18    13.9   3.15  9     21.0 within 
#> 5 MW2200      2200       14    13.9   3.11  8.95  21   within 
#> 6 MW2700      2700       12    13.7   3.03  8     20   within 
#> 7 MW3200      3200        5    11.8   2.76  6.95  17   below  
#> 8 MW3700      3700        2     7.65  2.59  3     13   below  
glance(mde)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   model   n_sites n_species    r2 p_value
#>   <chr>     <int>     <int> <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 uniform       8        55 0.354   0.055
